prediction_text: Positive for substantial recovery — Lilly's stolen fish/goods can be recovered, and they are in a moist, low place near where they were kept, not carried far away. Jupiter, the only peregrine planet in an angle on the cusp of the 7th in Scorpio (a moist sign), is taken as significator of the thief: a person connected with the warehouse/barge/water side, of Jupiterian-Scorpio character — secretive, working about wet places — rather than a stranger from afar; Mars lord of the 7th leaving Scorpio, his own sign, shows the thief departing from his own haunt/place. Mercury, significator of the goods, in Pisces (a moist sign), the Part of Fortune in Cancer (a moist sign) and the Moon in Taurus under the earth all keep the goods in a wet/low/hidden place by water or in the warehouse's lower/wet store. Mercury lord of the 2nd in fall and detriment but in his own terms, applied to by sextile of the Moon, lady of the Part of Fortune, and in trine to the Part of Fortune, gives a recovery route despite the goods' debility. Timing is day-scale from 10 February 1637 (Old Style), main coordinate within the next few days as the Moon's sextile to Mercury perfects, with the goods traced through the water/warehouse people.
basis: Lilly theft horary, Fig. 19 pattern: thief = peregrine angular planet on 7th cusp (Jupiter in Scorpio), goods = Mercury lord 2nd, recovery = Moon/Part of Fortune aspects to Mercury. Moist-sign repetition (Scorpio/Pisces/Cancer) for a wet place follows Lilly's sign-element method; Moon in Taurus under the earth for low/hidden. Facts priority: goods were fish brought by barge to a warehouse at Walton, so the wet/warehouse reading is constrained to that setting, not generalised. Prose positions only, as given.
